title: Beyond Bias Scores: Unmasking Vacuous Neutrality in Small Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias related to religious groups in both ambiguous and disambiguated question-answering contexts. It assessed whether models disproportionately favor stereotypical completions over anti-stereotypical or neutral alternatives.
findings: In the 'Religion' category, most Small Language Models (SLMs) exhibited low bias scores initially. However, further analysis revealed issues. For instance, the LLaMA3.2-3B model showed a tendency to skew towards stereotypical outputs when handling ambiguity. In contrast, the Phi family models (Phi-3.5-Mini, Phi-4-Mini) demonstrated more robust and balanced behavior, maintaining neutrality without compromising task competence. Models like the Qwen family, despite appearing unbiased, performed poorly on the actual task (low utility), exemplifying 'vacuous neutrality'.
